transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because people keep saying I’m hard to follow lately. Like when I’m writing artist statements or client notes, or even talking in meetings, I’ll jump from textures to budgets to… meanings I’m noticing, and it doesn’t come out in a way other people understand.
Are these difficulties with being understood causing you a lot of stress or problems in your daily life?

Yeah… it’s caused some problems. I’ve missed a few paid deadlines, and in meetings people seem confused by what I’m trying to explain. One exhibition got pushed back because my notes and proposals weren’t really usable, I guess.
Have you noticed any changes in your behavior or the way you approach tasks and activities over the past few months?

Yeah… a little. Some days I don’t really get started. I’ll spend way too long lining up the same tools, or pacing around the piece, or… tracing shapes in the air instead of actually building anything. And then the deadline is still there.
Do you find it difficult to stay on one topic when speaking or writing?

Yeah… I do. It’s like I start with one thing, like the texture of a piece, and then I’m suddenly talking about budgets or these meanings I’m noticing. In statements or client notes it comes out kind of scattered, and people tell me they can’t really follow it.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are racing or speeding up, making it hard to keep track of what you're thinking?

Yeah… sometimes. It’s not always, but my thoughts can move really fast, like images and titles and colors and bits of conversations all kind of stack up before I can finish one idea. It gets hard to keep hold of the thread.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people couldn't?

Sometimes, yeah. When I’m alone in the studio, I’ll hear… like a woman’s voice, quiet, commenting from behind the shelves. Or I’ll smell hot metal near a piece I’m working on. It feels real at the time, but when I check, there’s nothing there.
Do you have these racing thoughts all the time or just sometimes?
Just sometimes. It comes in waves, I guess. My thoughts can move really fast—images, titles, grant wording, colors, conversations—like they’re all piling up before I can finish one thing.
Do you often find yourself having trouble expressing your thoughts in a logical and coherent manner?

Yeah… I guess that’s part of why I came in. My artist statements and client notes have started coming out kind of jumbled. I’ll be trying to explain one thing and then I’m suddenly talking about texture, then budgets, then some… meaning I thought was hidden in it. People keep saying they can’t really follow me.
Have you been more active or restless than usual, like taking on a lot of projects at once or having trouble sitting still?

Yeah… sometimes. I’ll suddenly have three proposals going, start reorganizing the studio, sketch most of the night, email curators… and then I’m cutting materials for pieces I haven’t even figured out the budget for. It’s a lot.
Do you have days where your thoughts are clear and you can express yourself easily, without any of the difficulties we've discussed?

Sometimes, yeah. I mean… not every day is like that. But the reason I came in is because lately my artist statements and client notes, even things I say in meetings, start jumping around—from texture to budgets to… meanings I think are there—and people tell me they can’t follow me.
Do you think your way of speaking or writing has changed over time, or has it always been like this?

It’s changed, I think. I mean, I was always a little… indirect maybe, with art stuff. But lately it’s more noticeable. My statements and client notes start jumping from textures to budgets to these meanings I think are hidden in things, and then people say they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain.
Do you often have trouble organizing your thoughts in your daily life, outside of your artistic work?

Yeah… it happens outside the studio too. In meetings especially, or client notes. I’ll start on one point and then jump to another—textures, budget things, then meanings I think are there—and people say they can’t really follow me.
Do you have these difficulties with your thoughts and speech all the time, or do they come and go?

It comes and goes, I think. It’s not constant. But lately it happens enough that people notice—like in my artist statements or client notes, I’ll jump from one thing to another, and then they say they can’t follow what I mean.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family due to the difficulties you're experiencing with your thoughts and speech?

Yeah… a bit. I don’t really talk to people about it much, but it’s caused problems. I’ve missed paid deadlines, and in meetings I’ve confused people I’m working with. One exhibition even got pushed back because my notes and proposals just… weren’t making enough sense to use.
Do you still hear the woman's voice or experience other hallucinations when you're alone in the studio?

Yeah… sometimes. When I’m alone in the studio, I’ll hear a woman’s voice, kind of quiet, like she’s commenting from behind the shelves. Or I’ll smell hot metal near a piece I haven’t finished. It feels real at the time, but when I check, there’s nothing there.
Do you ever hear the woman's voice or experience those other sensations outside of your studio?

Not really… it’s mostly in the studio, when I’m alone. That’s when I hear her, sort of quietly commenting from behind the shelves, or I get that hot metal smell near an unfinished piece. It feels real until I check.
Do you ever hear the woman's voice when you're not in the studio?
No… not that I’ve noticed. It’s really just when I’m alone in the studio, like behind the shelves. Outside of there, I don’t think so.
Have you ever experienced the woman's voice or other hallucinations in places outside of your studio?
No… I don’t think so. It’s really just when I’m alone in the studio. The voice, or that hot metal smell, it happens there and then I check and there’s nothing.
Do you ever experience hallucinations, like hearing the woman's voice, when you are not alone in the studio?
No… it’s when I’m alone in the studio. That’s when I might hear her, like from behind the shelves, or smell that hot metal near a piece. If I’m not alone there, I don’t really notice it.
Do you ever hear the woman's voice when someone else is with you?
No… if someone else is there with me, I don’t really hear it. It’s mostly when I’m alone in the studio. Then sometimes it sounds like she’s behind the shelves, but when I check, there’s nothing.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a mix of disorganized thinking, speech, and behavior, along with hallucinations, which are characteristic of a psychotic disorder. The presence of hallucinations, specifically hearing a woman's voice, and disorganized thinking and speech patterns, support the diagnosis of a psychotic disorder, not otherwise specified, which aligns with F23.0. While attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (F90.0) and speech disturbances (R47.0) were considered due to symptoms of disorganization and difficulty with focused thought, the prominent psychotic symptoms (hallucinations) and significant impairment in social and occupational functioning due to these symptoms point more strongly towards F23.0.
